question_en:
I am helping the school's Geoscience Museum create a verifiable record for the specimen in the attachment. Please answer the following questions:

1. What is the museum collection record corresponding to the photo? Please provide the mineral name, collection institution, collection number, published locality, and dimensions.
2. Starting from the mineral in this collection record, what is its fluorine-bearing analogue called?
3. What are the ideal chemical formulas for these two minerals? What is the dominant F/OH relationship at the same anion site for each?
4. Where are the type localities for these two minerals? What are the holding institutions and numbers for their respective type specimens?

Answer Format: Please answer in points numbered (1)–(4). Each point should only answer the corresponding sub-question and provide all information required by that question. Answer points 1 and 2 in text, and use a separate comparison table for each of points 3 and 4.
answer:
(1) Mineral: Carletonite; Collection Institution: Canadian Museum of Nature; Collection Number: CMNMC 87519; Published Locality: Mont Saint-Hilaire, Québec, Canada; Dimensions: 6 × 9 cm.

(2) Fluorcarletonite.

(3)

| Mineral | Ideal Chemical Formula | Dominant F/OH Relationship at the Same Anion Site |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Carletonite | KNa4Ca4Si8O18(CO3)4(OH)·H2O | OH > F, OH dominant |
| Fluorcarletonite | KNa4Ca4Si8O18(CO3)4F·H2O | F > OH, F dominant |

(4)

| Mineral | Type Locality | Type Specimen Holding Institution | Type Specimen Number |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Carletonite | Mont Saint-Hilaire / Poudrette quarry, Québec, Canada | Canadian Museum of Nature | T711 |
| Fluorcarletonite | Severny district, Maly Murun syenite massif, NW Aldan Shield, Siberia, Russia | Sidorov State Mineralogical Museum, Irkutsk National Research Technical University | 12/1764 |

# Detailed Simulated Search Trajectory · P2-8-2-E01

## Step 01 · Establish the target object from the blue crystal photo

Action: Observe the blue tetragonal crystals and their aggregate morphology in the current input, and perform image comparison first. Example query: Canadian Museum of Nature Mont Saint-Hilaire blue tetragonal carletonite.

Evidence observation: Color and crystal habit provide only search clues; F/OH content or type specimen identity cannot be determined from the photo alone. The Carletonite photo in the museum's Mont Saint-Hilaire special topic corresponds to the main subject of the question image; adjacent figure captions must be read next.

Evidence links:
https://nature.ca/en/mont-saint-hilaire-at-cmn-at-the-heart-of-canadas-mineral-collection/
https://nature.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/blog_Carletonite.jpg

Result of this step: Found the same photo record with collection number and dimensions.

## Step 02 · Extract identity fields from the photo caption

Action: Itemize and extract the mineral name, institution, number, published locality, and dimensions from the museum's photo page, keeping the photo record separate from subsequent species classification data.

Evidence observation: Mineral Carletonite; Institution Canadian Museum of Nature; Photo specimen number CMNMC 87519; Published locality Mont Saint-Hilaire, Québec, Canada; Dimensions 6 × 9 cm. The individual number in the photo does not mean it is the type specimen originally described for this species.

Evidence links:
https://nature.ca/en/mont-saint-hilaire-at-cmn-at-the-heart-of-canadas-mineral-collection/
https://nature.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/blog_Carletonite.jpg

Result of this step: The five fields for Question 1 are determined; use the mineral name carletonite as the search bridge for subsequent steps.

## Step 03 · Trace back to the original description of carletonite

Action: Example query: Chao 1971 carletonite type specimen T711 American Mineralogist. Locate the 1971 original description and verify the mineral name and locality.

Evidence observation: Chao's original article was published in American Mineralogist 56, pages 1855–1866, describing a mineral from Mount St. Hilaire. The original text states the type specimen is held at the then National Museum of Canada, number T711; this is not the same field as the photo specimen CMNMC 87519.

Evidence links:
https://msaweb.org/AmMin/AM56/AM56_1855.pdf

Result of this step: Extracted the historical type specimen number and clues to the original locality.

## Step 04 · Verify the current holding institution name using a mineral handbook

Action: Open the Handbook of Mineralogy entry and locate Type Material and Distribution.

Evidence observation: Type Material lists Canadian Museum of Nature, Ottawa, Canada, T711; Distribution corresponds to Mont Saint-Hilaire, Québec. The handbook connects the historical institution name in the original literature to the current institution name; do not fabricate another type specimen due to the name change.

Evidence links:
https://www.handbookofmineralogy.org/pdfs/carletonite.pdf
https://msaweb.org/AmMin/AM56/AM56_1855.pdf

Result of this step: The Carletonite type specimen holding institution and T711 receive cross-support.

## Step 05 · Search for the new mineral name along the fluorine-bearing analogue relationship

Action: Example query: carletonite F-dominant analogue fluorcarletonite IMA 2019-038. Enter the corresponding entry in IMA-CNMNC Newsletter No.51.

Evidence observation: IMA No.2019-038 is named Fluorcarletonite and is explicitly called the F-dominant analogue of carletonite. The prefix fluor- is not a name added based on color; it must match the approval record.

Evidence links:
https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/mineralogical-magazine/article/new-minerals-and-nomenclature-modifications-approved-in-2019/28CA10A2688F6377D683AC1C76A64D32

Result of this step: The name for Question 2 is Fluorcarletonite.

## Step 06 · Read the chemical formula from the fluorcarletonite approval entry

Action: Compare the ideal formula in the IMA entry with subsequent formal paper citations, preserving the water of crystallization and bracket subscript relationships.

Evidence observation: The approval entry gives KNa4Ca4Si8O18(CO3)4F·H2O; do not write non-integer site occupancies measured in samples as the ideal end-member. The naming basis is F dominance at the corresponding anion site, not that element F has the greatest mass in the entire sample.

Evidence links:
https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/mineralogical-magazine/article/new-minerals-and-nomenclature-modifications-approved-in-2019/28CA10A2688F6377D683AC1C76A64D32
https://ejm.copernicus.org/articles/32/137/2020/ejm-32-137-2020.pdf

Result of this step: Fixed the F end-member ideal formula; continue to check the OH end-member boundary.

## Step 07 · Use the 2020 paper to explain the F/OH coexistence in the old chemical formula

Action: In the Kaneva et al. 2020 paper, check the discussion of carletonite and site occupancy at the same anion site, distinguishing the old notation (F,OH) from modern end-member expressions.

Evidence observation: The paper discusses old carletonite samples with F0.41(OH)0.59, where OH > F; therefore, the modern carletonite ideal end-member uses (OH), and the Fluorcarletonite end-member uses F. The order of (F,OH) in early formulas cannot be reversed to serve as proof of F dominance.

Evidence links:
https://ejm.copernicus.org/articles/32/137/2020/ejm-32-137-2020.pdf
https://msaweb.org/AmMin/AM56/AM56_1855.pdf
https://www.handbookofmineralogy.org/pdfs/carletonite.pdf

Result of this step: The two minerals are distinguished by the OH/F dominance relationship at the same site.

## Step 08 · Establish a comparison of ideal end-members for the two minerals

Action: Check K, Na, Ca, Si, O, carbonate, the anion site, and water of crystallization one by one; do not infer composition from the photo appearance.

Evidence observation: The common framework KNa4Ca4Si8O18(CO3)4 and ·H2O are retained; the Carletonite site is OH, with OH > F; the Fluorcarletonite site is F, with F > OH. The ideal formulas are KNa4Ca4Si8O18(CO3)4(OH)·H2O and KNa4Ca4Si8O18(CO3)4F·H2O, respectively.

Evidence links:
https://ejm.copernicus.org/articles/32/137/2020/ejm-32-137-2020.pdf
https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/mineralogical-magazine/article/new-minerals-and-nomenclature-modifications-approved-in-2019/28CA10A2688F6377D683AC1C76A64D32

Result of this step: Question 3 can be constructed as a two-row comparison table.

## Step 09 · Distinguish between the photo's published locality and the carletonite type locality

Action: Return to the original description and handbook to verify the type locality expressions for Mont Saint-Hilaire and Poudrette quarry.

Evidence observation: The Carletonite type locality is Mont Saint-Hilaire / Poudrette quarry, Québec, Canada. The photo is also labeled Mont Saint-Hilaire, but the same place name does not mean the photo specimen is T711; for Question 1 still use CMNMC 87519, and for Question 4 use T711.

Evidence links:
https://nature.ca/en/mont-saint-hilaire-at-cmn-at-the-heart-of-canadas-mineral-collection/
https://msaweb.org/AmMin/AM56/AM56_1855.pdf
https://www.handbookofmineralogy.org/pdfs/carletonite.pdf
https://ejm.copernicus.org/articles/32/137/2020/ejm-32-137-2020.pdf

Result of this step: The locality, institution, and type specimen number for the Canada row are each assigned correctly.

## Step 10 · Look up the complete type locality for the Russian analogue

Action: Read the complete regional hierarchy from the Geological context in the IMA entry and the 2020 paper.

Evidence observation: The Fluorcarletonite type locality is Severny district, Maly Murun syenite massif, NW Aldan Shield, Siberia, Russia. Do not copy carletonite's Canadian locality to the fluorine-bearing species; the approval entry also provides latitude and longitude for location verification.

Evidence links:
https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/mineralogical-magazine/article/new-minerals-and-nomenclature-modifications-approved-in-2019/28CA10A2688F6377D683AC1C76A64D32
https://ejm.copernicus.org/articles/32/137/2020/ejm-32-137-2020.pdf

Result of this step: The Russian location serves as the type locality for the second mineral.

## Step 11 · Verify the holotype custody record for fluorcarletonite

Action: Check the holotype and catalogue number in the introductory section of the 2020 paper, and cross-validate with the IMA entry.

Evidence observation: The holotype is held at Sidorov State Mineralogical Museum, Irkutsk National Research Technical University, catalogue no.12/1764. Number 12/1764 is not the mineral approval number IMA2019-038, nor is it the photo's CMNMC87519.

Evidence links:
https://ejm.copernicus.org/articles/32/137/2020/ejm-32-137-2020.pdf
https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/mineralogical-magazine/article/new-minerals-and-nomenclature-modifications-approved-in-2019/28CA10A2688F6377D683AC1C76A64D32

Result of this step: The three fields for the second row of Question 4 are complete.

## Step 12 · Check the entire search chain according to source responsibilities

Action: Map the museum photo page, original description, mineral handbook, approval announcement, and 2020 paper respectively to the answer fields.

Evidence observation: S01 supports the specimen in the photo; S02/S03 support the carletonite type specimen; S04/S05 support the new mineral naming, F-dominant end-member, and Russian type specimen; S05 clarifies the OH/F boundary between the two end-members. The five sources are complementary; all four questions cannot be deduced from the museum photo page alone.

Evidence links:
https://nature.ca/en/mont-saint-hilaire-at-cmn-at-the-heart-of-canadas-mineral-collection/
https://msaweb.org/AmMin/AM56/AM56_1855.pdf
https://www.handbookofmineralogy.org/pdfs/carletonite.pdf
https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/mineralogical-magazine/article/new-minerals-and-nomenclature-modifications-approved-in-2019/28CA10A2688F6377D683AC1C76A64D32
https://ejm.copernicus.org/articles/32/137/2020/ejm-32-137-2020.pdf

Result of this step: The three numbering systems and the two localities remain clearly distinguished.

## Step 13 · Verify question requirements and output scope

Action: Correspond each publicly required item with the above evidence one by one, checking the total count, positive/negative items, and field formats.

Evidence observation: Questions 1 and 2 in text; Questions 3 and 4 each as a two-row comparison table; chemical formulas adopt modern ideal end-members; no evidence-free chemical assay inferences were made for the photo specimen.

Result of this step: Only the requested information is written into the final answer; the search process and exclusion basis are retained in the trajectory.

## Step 14 · Final Answer

(1) Mineral: Carletonite; Collection Institution: Canadian Museum of Nature; Collection Number: CMNMC 87519; Published Locality: Mont Saint-Hilaire, Québec, Canada; Dimensions: 6 × 9 cm.

（2）Fluorcarletonite。

（3）

| Fluorcarletonite | KNa4Ca4Si8O18(CO3)4F·H2O | F > OH, F dominant |

（4）

| Mineral | Type Locality | Type Specimen Holding Institution | Type Specimen Number |
